rationales: Fourth and fifth periods are not classified as short periods.
They are not called normal periods.
The fourth and fifth periods are long periods.
The sixth and seventh periods are called very long periods.
Nitrogen molecules contain a triple covalent bond.
Oxygen molecules contain a double covalent bond.
Hydrogen molecules contain a single covalent bond.
Chlorine molecules contain a single covalent bond.
NH₃ has a complete octet around its nitrogen atom.
N₂ has complete octets through its triple bond.
BF₃ is electron deficient because boron has only six electrons around it.
O₂ has complete octets in its usual Lewis structure.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass among these gases and diffuses fastest.
Helium is heavier than hydrogen, so it diffuses more slowly.
Fluorine is much heavier than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
Chlorine is the heaviest listed gas and diffuses most slowly.
Toothpaste is generally treated as a colloid or gel, not a suspension in this classification.
Milk is a colloid.
Chalk particles dispersed in water form a suspension.
Blood is commonly classified as a colloid in this context, not the intended example of a suspension.
Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, represented as Fe₂O₃·nH₂O.
Fe₂O₃ alone omits the water of hydration in rust.
Fe(OH)₃ is not the standard formula used for rust.
Fe(OH)₃·nH₂O is not the standard formula for rust.
Alkali metals have the general outer configuration ns¹.
Alkaline earth metals have the general outer configuration ns².
The boron family generally has the configuration ns²np¹.
The carbon family generally has the configuration ns²np².
Ion making is not the general result of dominant attractive forces between atoms.
Bond breakage occurs when a bond is disrupted, not when attraction dominates.
Dominant attractive forces between atoms lead to bond formation.
Polarity describes unequal charge distribution and is not the general result described.
Eight electrons are not shared in a triple covalent bond.
A triple covalent bond consists of three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Four electrons correspond to two shared pairs, forming a double bond.
Five electrons cannot make up three shared electron pairs.
Milk of magnesia is not a true solution because magnesium hydroxide is only sparingly soluble.
It is generally classified as a suspension rather than a colloid in this context.
Saturated solution is not the usual classification of milk of magnesia.
Undissolved magnesium hydroxide particles dispersed in water make milk of magnesia a suspension.
For equal volumes of solution, 2 M is the most concentrated and is the intended choice for having less water relative to solute.
A 1 M solution is less concentrated than a 2 M solution.
A 0.5 M solution is less concentrated than a 1 M solution.
A 0.25 M solution is the least concentrated of these options.
Oxidation alone does not describe the whole reaction because carbon is oxidized while zinc oxide is reduced.
Reduction alone does not describe the whole reaction because carbon is also oxidized.
The reaction is redox: carbon is oxidized and zinc oxide is reduced.
No electrolysis is involved because the reaction is not driven by an electric current.
Sulphuric acid solution conducts electricity through mobile ions and is an electrolyte.
Sugar dissolves without forming ions, so sugar solution is not an electrolyte.
Calcium hydroxide solution contains ions and conducts electricity, so it is an electrolyte.
Sodium chloride solution contains mobile ions and is an electrolyte.
Potassium is highly reactive.
Aluminium is more reactive than silver.
Lead is more reactive than silver.
Silver is the least reactive metal among these options.
H₂O₃ is not the formula of hydrogen peroxide.
Hydrogen peroxide has the formula H₂O₂.
H₂O is the formula of water.
HO is not the molecular formula of hydrogen peroxide.
